# jq-pointer

> Paste JSON, click the value you want, get the jq expression that extracts it - the reverse of every jq playground.
> Fully client-side: the JSON never leaves the browser and never appears in the URL.

## How to use

- Paste JSON into the input box, or drop a file onto it (capped at ~10MB).
  The document renders as a collapsible, virtualised tree.
- Paste newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) and the tool detects it automatically when at least 90% of two or more non-empty lines parse.
  Each record is navigable with the Previous/Next record controls, which report "Record N/M (line L)".
  Malformed lines are listed as positioned errors alongside the controls.
- Click one value to get its exact jq path with correct quoting (`."foo-bar"`), array indices, and top-level `.`.
- Click the counterpart value in a sibling array element and the tool detects the common array ancestor and generalises to the iterator expression (`.items[].name`).
  When not every element contains the clicked key-path, the `?` form is emitted with a "matches N of M elements" note.
- Select different keys of the same element to get flat shorthand object construction (`.items[] | {name, id}`).
  Selected nodes appear as removable chips; clicks toggle membership.
- When more than one ancestor array could be iterated, a breadcrumb widens the generalisation to outer arrays (e.g. `.data[].items[].name`).
- The Copy button puts the bare jq expression on the clipboard.
  On NDJSON input two shell-ready invocations are offered instead - "Copy per-line" (`jq '<expression>'`, run per record) and "Copy slurped" (`jq -s`, with the expression applied per array element, e.g. `.items[].name` becomes `.[].items[].name`).
- Paste a jq expression from the tool's own path/iterator/construction grammar into the highlight box and the matching nodes highlight in the tree.
  Anything outside that grammar shows an explicit "Can't preview this filter." state - there is no arbitrary jq evaluation.
- Clicks with no common pattern (different key-paths across elements, or across different arrays) are kept as separate outputs with a visible "No common pattern between these clicks; showing each path separately." note.

## Input handling

Parsing is strict `JSON.parse` with no tolerant repair.
Errors show the position and a caret excerpt.
Valid NDJSON input is not an error - it parses to a navigable record stream.
JavaScript-literal pastes are detected heuristically and named in the error message without repair.

Two `JSON.parse` behaviours are inherited deliberately, with no warning:

- Duplicate keys: the last occurrence wins.
  `{"a": 1, "a": 2}` parses as `{"a": 2}` and paths address only the surviving value.
- Number precision: numbers beyond IEEE 754 double precision lose precision.
  `9007199254740993` parses as `9007199254740992`.

## Privacy

No accounts, no analytics, no third-party requests.
All processing happens in the browser; the URL never contains the document.
